_note: Every quote is cut from data/laws/text/<doc>.pages.json by tools; tests/test_law_quotes.py re-checks each one. 'gist' and 'practice_note' are plain-language explanations, not law text.

entries.chapter: Chapter II - Registration of real estate project
entries.title: Projects must be registered with RERA
quote: 3. (1) No promoter shall advertise, market, book, sell or offer for sale, or invite persons to purchase in any manner any plot, apartment or building, as the case may be, in any real estate project or part of it, in any planning area, without registering the real estate project with the Real Estate Regulatory Authority established under this Act
entries.gist: A builder cannot advertise, book or sell flats in a project without first registering it with RERA.

entries.chapter: Chapter II - Registration of real estate project
entries.title: Small projects that need no registration
quote: (2) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1), no registration of the real estate project shall be required- (a) where the area of land proposed to be developed does not exceed five hundred square meters or the number of apartments proposed to be developed does not exceed eight inclusive of all phases
entries.gist: Registration is not needed if the land is 500 sq m or less, or the project has 8 or fewer apartments in all phases.

entries.chapter: Chapter II - Registration of real estate project
entries.title: Meaning of force majeure
quote: Explanation.- For the purpose of this section, the expression "force majeure" shall mean a case of war, flood, drought, fire, cyclone, earthquake or any other calamity caused by nature affecting the regular development of the real estate project.
entries.gist: Under RERA, 'force majeure' means war, flood, drought, fire, cyclone, earthquake or another natural calamity that affects the project. Whether a builder's excuse counts is for TG-RERA to decide.

entries.chapter: Chapter III - Functions and duties of promoter
entries.title: Builder stays responsible until conveyance
quote: (4) The promoter shall- (a) be responsible for all obligations, responsibilties and functions under the provisions of this Act or the rules and regulations made thereunder or to the allottees as per the agreement for sale, or to the association of allottees, as the case may be, till the conveyance of all the apartments, plots or buildings, as the case may be, to the allottees, or the common areas to the association of allottees or the competent authority, as the case may be:
entries.gist: The builder remains responsible for everything promised in the agreement for sale until the flats (and common areas) are conveyed.

entries.chapter: Chapter III - Functions and duties of promoter
entries.title: No more than 10% advance without a registered agreement
quote: 13. (1) A promoter shall not accept a sum more than ten per cent of the cost of the apartment, plot, or building as the case may be, as an advance payment or an application fee, from a person without first entering into a written agreement for sale with such person and register the said agreement for sale, under any law for the time being in force.
entries.gist: A builder cannot take more than 10% of the price as advance before signing and registering an agreement for sale.

entries.chapter: Chapter III - Functions and duties of promoter
entries.title: Defects reported within 5 years must be fixed in 30 days
quote: (3) In case any structural defect or any other defect in workmanship, quality or provision of services or any other obligations of the promoter as per the agreement for sale relating to such development is brought to the notice of the promoter within a period of five years by the allottee from the date of handing over possession, it shall be the duty of the promoter to rectify such defects without further charge, within thirty days, and in the event of promoter's failure to rectify such defects within such time, the aggrieved allottees shall be entitled to receive appropriate compensation in the manner as provided under this Act.
entries.gist: If you report a structural defect or poor workmanship, quality or services to the builder within 5 years of getting possession, the builder must fix it free within 30 days; if not, you can claim compensation.

entries.chapter: Chapter III - Functions and duties of promoter
entries.title: Delay in possession: refund with interest, or interest for every month of delay
quote: 18. (1) If the promoter fails to complete or is unable to give possession of an apartment, plot or building,- (a) in accordance with the terms of the agreement for sale or, as the case may be, duly completed by the date specified therein; or (b) due to discontinuance of his business as a developer on account of suspension or revocation of the registration under this Act or for any other reason, he shall be liable on demand to the allottees, in case the allottee wishes to withdraw from the project, without prejudice to any other remedy available, to return the amount received by him in respect of that apartment, plot, building, as the case may be, with interest at such rate as may be prescribed in this behalf including compensation in the manner as provided under this Act: Provided that where an allottee does not intend to withdraw from the project, he shall be paid, by the promoter, interest for every month of delay, till the handing over of the possession, at such rate as may be prescribed.
entries.gist: If the builder does not give possession by the date in the agreement, you can either withdraw and get your money back with interest (plus compensation), or stay in the project and get interest for every month of delay until handover.

entries.chapter: Chapter IV - Rights and duties of allottees
entries.title: Buyer's right to refund with interest and compensation
quote: (4) The allottee shall be entitled to claim the refund of amount paid along with interest at such rate as may be prescribed and compensation in the manner as provided under this Act, from the promoter, if the promoter fails to comply or is unable to give possession of the apartment, plot or building, as the case may be, in accordance with the terms of agreement for sale or due to discontinuance of his business as a developer on account of suspension or revocation of his registration under the provisions of this Act or the rules or regulations made thereunder.
entries.gist: A buyer can claim a refund with interest and compensation if the builder fails to give possession as agreed.

entries.chapter: Chapter IV - Rights and duties of allottees
entries.title: Buyer must also pay on time
quote: (7) The allottee shall be liable to pay interest, at such rate as may be prescribed, for any delay in payment towards any amount or charges to be paid under sub-section (6).
entries.gist: If the buyer delays their own payments, the buyer also owes interest at the prescribed rate.

entries.chapter: Chapter VII - Offences, penalties and adjudication (complaints)
entries.title: Who can file a complaint, and where
quote: 31. (1) Any aggrieved person may file a complaint with the Authority or the adjudicating officer, as the case may be, for any violation or contravention of the provisions of this Act or the rules and regulations made thereunder against any promoter allottee or real estate agent, as the cae may be. Explanation.-For the purpose of this sub-section "person" shall include the association of allottees or any voluntary consumer association registered under any law for the time being in force.
entries.gist: Any aggrieved buyer (or an association of buyers) can file a complaint with the Authority or the adjudicating officer.

entries.chapter: Chapter V - Real Estate Regulatory Authority
entries.title: Recovering money the builder is ordered to pay
quote: 40. (1) If a promoter or an allottee or a real estate agent, as the case may be, fails to pay any interest or penalty or compensation imposed on him, by the adjudicating officer or the Regulatory Authority or the Appellate Authority, as the case may be, under this Act or the rules and regualtions made thereunder, it shall be recoverable from such promoter or allottee or real estate agent, in such manner as may be prescribed as an arrears of land revenue.
entries.gist: If the builder does not pay interest or compensation ordered by RERA, it can be recovered from the builder like arrears of land revenue.

entries.title: Builder must deposit before appealing
quote: Provided that where a promoter files an appeal with the Appellate Tribunal, it shall not be entertatined, without the prmoter first having deposited with the Appellate Tribunal atleast thirty per cent. of the penalty, or such higher percentage as may be determined by the Appellate Tribunal, or the total amount to be paid to the allottee including interest and compensation imposed on him, if any, or with both, as the case may be, before the said appeal is heard.
entries.gist: A builder who appeals a RERA order must first deposit at least 30% of the penalty, or the full amount payable to the buyer, with the Appellate Tribunal.

entries.title: Time limit to appeal: 60 days
quote: (2) Every appeal made under sub-section (1) shall be preferred within a period of sixty days from the date on which a copy of the direction or order or decision made by the Authority or the adjudicating officer is received by the appropriate Government or the competent authority or the aggrieved person and it shall be in such form and accompanied by such fee, as may be prescribed:
entries.gist: An appeal against a RERA order must be filed within 60 days of receiving a copy of the order.

entries.chapter: Chapter VIII - Offences, penalties and adjudication
entries.title: Compensation is decided by the adjudicating officer
quote: 71. (1) For the purpose of adjudging compensation under sections 12, 14, 18 and section 19, the Authority shall appoint in consultation with the appropriate Government one or more judicial officer as deemed necessary, who is or has been a District Judge to be an adjudicating officer for holding an inquiry in the prescribed manner, after giving any person concerned a reasonable opportunity of being heard:
entries.gist: Compensation claims (for delay, defects and other violations) are decided by an adjudicating officer, a serving or former District Judge.

entries.chapter: Chapter VIII - Offences, penalties and adjudication
entries.title: What decides the amount of compensation
quote: 72. While adjudging the quantum of compensation or interest, as the case may be, under section 71, the adjudicating officer shall have due regard to the following factors, namely:- (a) the amount of disproportionate gain or unfair advantage, wherever quantifiable, made as a result of the default;

(b) the amount of loss caused as a result of the default; (c) the repetitive nature of the default; (d) such other factors which the adjudicating officer considers necessary to the case in furtherance of justice.
entries.gist: The officer looks at the builder's unfair gain, your loss, whether the default is repeated, and other relevant factors. There is no fixed formula, so the bot does not estimate compensation.

entries.title: Civil courts cannot hear RERA matters
quote: 79. No civil court shall have jurisdiction to entertain any suit or proceeding in respect of any matter which the Authority or the adjudicating officer or the Appellate Tribunal is empowered by or under this Act to determine and no injunction shall be granted by any court or other authority in respect of any action taken or to be taken in pursuance of any power conferred by or under this Act.
entries.gist: A civil court cannot hear a suit on matters RERA can decide. (This bars civil courts, not consumer commissions.)

entries.title: Other laws still apply
quote: 88. The provisions of this Act shall be in addition to, and not in derogation of, the provisions of any other law for the time being in force.
entries.gist: RERA adds to other laws; it does not replace them. So other routes, such as a consumer commission, can remain open.

entries.title: Interest rate in Telangana: highest SBI MCLR + 2%
quote: 15. Interest payable by promoter and allottee.- The rate of interest payable by the promoter to the allottee or by the allottee to the promoter, as the case may be, shall be highest Marginal Cost of Lending Rate of State Bank of India plus two per cent. Provided that in case the Marginal Cost of Lending Rate of State Bank of India is not in use it would be replaced by such benchmark lending rates which the State Bank of India may fix from time to time for lending to the general public.
entries.gist: In Telangana, interest owed by the builder (or the buyer) is SBI's highest Marginal Cost of Lending Rate plus 2% a year. The final rate and period are set by the order in your case.

entries.title: Projects approved before 01.01.2017 are excluded
quote: Ongoing Project" means, a Project where development is going on and for which Occupancy Certificate or Completion Certificate has not been issued but excludes such Projects for which building permissions were approved prior to 01.01.2017 by the Competent Authorities viz., UDAs / DTCP / Municipal Corporations / Municipalities / Nagar Panchayats / TSIIC as the case may be.
entries.gist: In Telangana, an 'ongoing project' (one that must register) excludes projects whose building permission was approved before 1 January 2017.

entries.title: Complaint to TG-RERA (Form M)
quote: (1) Any aggrieved person may file a complaint with the Authority for any violation under the Act or the rules and regulations made thereunder, save as those provided to be adjudicated by the adjudicating officer, in Form 'M' annexed to this order, in triplicate, until the application procedure is made web based, which shall be accompanied by a fees of one thousand rupees in the form of either a demand draft or a bankers cheque drawn on a scheduled bank in favour of Authority and payable at the branch of that bank
entries.gist: A complaint to the Authority is made in Form 'M' with a fee of Rs 1,000. The portal now takes complaints online.
entries.practice_note: The Rule's text sends interest and compensation claims to the adjudicating officer (Form N). Since a 2021 Supreme Court ruling, refund and delay-interest complaints are decided by the Authority (Form M), and compensation by the adjudicating officer (Form N). A lawyer, or the TG-RERA complaint page, can confirm the route for your case.

entries.title: Claim to the adjudicating officer (Form N)
quote: (1) Any aggrieved person may file a complaint with the adjudicating officer for interest and compensation as provided under section 12, 14, 18 and 19 in Form 'N', in triplicate, until the application procedure is made web based, which shall be accompanied by a fees of one thousand rupees either in the form of a demand draft or a bankers cheque drawn on a scheduled bank in favour of the Authority and payable at the branch of that bank at the station where the seat of the said Authority is situated or through online payment, as the case may be.
entries.gist: A claim to the adjudicating officer is made in Form 'N' with a fee of Rs 1,000.
entries.practice_note: The Rule's text sends interest and compensation claims here (Form N). Since a 2021 Supreme Court ruling, refund and delay-interest complaints are decided by the Authority (Form M), and compensation by the adjudicating officer (Form N). A lawyer, or the TG-RERA complaint page, can confirm the route for your case.

entries.title: Defect liability and its exclusions
quote: 2. Notwithstanding anything contained in the above clause the following exclusions are made a. Equipment (lifts, generator, motors, STP, transformers, gym equipment etc) which carry manufacturer's guarantees for a limited period. Thereafter the welfare association /society shall take annual maintenance contract with the suppliers. The Promoter shall transfer manufacturers guarantees/warrantees to the allottee or association of allottees as the case may be. b. Fittings related to plumbing, sanitary, electrical, hardware, etc. having natural wear and tear. c. Allowable structural and other deformations including expansion quotient. d. The terms of work like painting etc. which are subject to wear and tear.
entries.gist: The Telangana model agreement excludes from free repair: equipment under the maker's guarantee (lifts, generators, motors etc.), fittings with natural wear and tear, allowable structural deformations, and painting-type wear.

entries.title: How to check if a project is registered
quote: Ans: The Flat/Plot Buyer should visit TG RERA website which would display all the registered projects. It is mandatory that the advertisement for marketing of flats/Plots in the real estate project must carry the TG RERA registration number.
entries.gist: Check the TG-RERA website for the project; its ads must show the TG-RERA registration number.

entries.title: Delay interest should be paid automatically
quote: Ans: The interest payment is in accordance with the agreement and hence should be automatically paid. The buyer may have to file a complaint to TG RERA if there is a grievance/ fail to comply.
entries.gist: TG-RERA's FAQ says delay interest should be paid automatically under the agreement; if not, the buyer may file a complaint.

entries.title: Agreement signed before registration can still complain
quote: Ans: TG RERA empowers any aggrieved person to file a complaint with respect to a registered real estate project.
entries.gist: TG-RERA says any aggrieved person, including a buyer whose agreement was signed before the project registered, can complain about a registered project.

entries.title: Who is a 'consumer' (services)
quote: (ii) hires or avails of any service for a consideration which has been paid or promised or partly paid and partly promised, or under any system of deferred payment and includes any beneficiary of such service other than the person who hires or avails of the services for consideration paid or promised, or partly paid and partly promised, or under any system of deferred payment, when such services are availed of with the approval of the first mentioned person, but does not include a person who avails of such service for any commercial purpose.
entries.gist: A buyer who pays for a service is a consumer, but not if it is for a commercial purpose (for example, buying flats as an investment business).

entries.title: 'Service' includes housing construction
quote: (42) "service" means service of any description which is made available to potential users and includes, but not limited to, the provision of facilities in connection with banking, financing, insurance, transport, processing, supply of electrical or other energy, telecom, boarding or lodging or both, housing construction, entertainment, amusement or the purveying of news or other information, but does not include the rendering of any service free of charge or under a contract of personal service;
entries.gist: Housing construction counts as a 'service', so a homebuyer can use a consumer commission for deficient service.

entries.title: What 'deficiency' in service means
quote: (11) "deficiency" means any fault, imperfection, shortcoming or inadequacy in the quality, nature and manner of performance which is required to be maintained by or under any law for the time being in force or has been undertaken to be performed by a person in pursuance of a contract or otherwise in relation to any service and includes- (i) any act of negligence or omission or commission by such person which causes loss or injury to the consumer;
entries.gist: A 'deficiency' is any fault or shortcoming in the quality or manner of a service promised under a contract or required by law.

entries.title: You can file in the district where you live
quote: (c) the cause of action, wholly or in part, arises; or (d) the complainant resides or personally works for gain.
entries.gist: A consumer complaint can be filed in the district where the cause of action arose, or where you live or work.

entries.title: Two-year limit for consumer complaints
quote: 69. (1) The District Commission, the State Commission or the National Commission shall not admit a complaint unless it is filed within two years from the date on which the cause of action has arisen.
entries.gist: A consumer complaint must normally be filed within 2 years of the cause of action. When that period starts for a delay case is a legal question a lawyer should confirm.

entries.title: Which consumer commission: by amount paid
quote: 3. Jurisdiction of District Commission.-Subject to the other provisions of the Act and in pursuance of proviso to sub-section (1) of section 34 of the Act, the District Commission shall have jurisdiction to entertain complaints where the value of the goods or services paid as consideration does not exceed fifty lakh rupees.

4. Jurisdiction of State Commission.-Subject to the other provisions of the Act and in pursuance of proviso to sub-clause (i) of clause (a) of sub-section (1) of section 47, the State Commission shall have jurisdiction to entertain complaints where the value of the goods or services paid as consideration exceeds fifty lakh but does not exceed two crore rupees.

5. Jurisdiction of National Commission.-Subject to the other provisions of the Act and in pursuance of proviso to sub-clause (i) of clause (a) of sub-section (1) of section 58, the National Commission shall have jurisdiction to entertain complaints where the value of the goods or services paid as consideration, exceeds two crore rupees.
entries.gist: The commission depends on the value paid as consideration: up to Rs 50 lakh, District; above Rs 50 lakh up to Rs 2 crore, State; above Rs 2 crore, National.

entries.chapter: Legal Services Authorities Act - Chapter IV
entries.title: Who gets free legal services
quote: Every person who has to file or defend a case shall be entitled to legal services under this Act if that person, is(a) A member of a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe; (b) A victim of trafficking in human beings or beggar as referred to in Article 23 of the Constitution; (c) A women or a child; [(d) A person with disability as defined in clause (i) of section 2 of the Persons with Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act, 1995 (1 of 1996);] (e) A person under circumstances of undeserved want such as being a victim of a mass disaster, ethnic violence, caste atrocity, flood, drought, earthquake or industrial disaster; or (f) An industrial workman; or

(h) in receipt of annual income less than rupees nine thousand or such other higher amount as may be prescribed by the State Government, if the case is before a court other than the Supreme Court, and less than rupees twelve thousand or such other higher amount as may be prescribed by the Central Government, if the case is before the Supreme Court.]
entries.gist: Free legal services are for, among others, SC/ST members, women, children, persons with disability, disaster victims, industrial workers, and people below an income limit that each state sets. The DLSA confirms eligibility; anyone can get basic legal advice there.
